morphology.shape: Diplococci — kidney-bean/coffee-bean shaped with flattened adjacent sides
morphology.capsule: Polysaccharide capsule (serogroups A, B, C, W, Y, and others)

habitat.hostAssociation: Asymptomatic nasopharyngeal carriage in a portion of the population; invasive disease occurs in a minority of colonized individuals

microscopy.appearance: Gram-negative diplococci, often seen intracellularly within neutrophils in CSF during meningitis

culture.media: Chocolate agar or Thayer-Martin medium, incubated with 5-10% CO2
culture.colonyMorphology: Small, gray, glistening, mucoid colonies (encapsulated strains)
culture.hemolysis: Not applicable — grown on enriched, non-blood media

identificationClues: Ferments both glucose and maltose — distinguishes it from N. gonorrhoeae, which does not ferment maltose
Intracellular diplococci on CSF Gram stain during meningitis

diseases: Meningococcemia, which can progress to purpura fulminans
Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome (adrenal hemorrhage in fulminant disease)
virulenceFactors: Polysaccharide capsule — antiphagocytic, and the basis of serogrouping
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Can cause epidemic meningitis, notably in the African meningitis belt; conjugate vaccines target the major capsular serogroups
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: CSF Gram stain showing Gram-negative diplococci, together with culture and PCR, supports diagnosis; rapid identification is critical given the fulminant course of invasive disease

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Oxidase positive; ferments both glucose and maltose
examFacts.importantTest: CSF Gram stain and culture; maltose fermentation test
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Maltose-fermenting, distinguishing it from N. gonorrhoeae, plus a prominent polysaccharide capsule
